newsitem.title: USA: Congressman threatens subpoena of papers.
newsitem.headline: Congressman threatens subpoena of papers.

text.p: A congressional subcommittee chairman investigating a White House data base threatened Tuesday to subpoena the information he seeks unless he gets it voluntarily.

Representative David McIntosh, an Indiana Republican who heads a subcommittee of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, released a letter written to White House counsel Charles Ruff urging him to turn over information from the data base.

McIntosh has been investigating whether the tax-financed White House data base of thousands of names were used for fund-raising or other political purposes. The White House has denied the data base were used improperly.

Ruff responded to an earlier request for information about attendees at White House events, such as dinners and movies, with a proposal to let subcommittee staffers look at some data at the White House to determine which events were solely personal.

In his letter released Tuesday, McIntosh turned Ruff down saying "the process would signficantly diminish the subcommittee's ability to re-examine records on the basis of information obtained subsequent to the conclusion of the process."

"Therefore I must ask again for a new copy of the data base as set forth in my March 21, 1997 letter to you," McIntosh replied. "If you will not produce it, despite the numerous requests since last July, I will have no other choice but to seek a subpoena."
McIntosh also asked for full copies of certain legal letters that were turned over to the subcommittee but which were censored.
While he asked Ruff to send the documents to the subcommittee by noon Tuesday, the subcommittee's senior counsel said the White House did not transfer the papers.
McIntosh serves on the committee headed by Representative Dan Burton, another Indiania Republican, who was investigating the campaign funding tactics of President Clinton's Democrats.
Also on Tuesday, Burton scheduled a long-delayed public hearing of the full committee for this Thursday to discuss the scope and budget of the investigation.
